title: Multitime Scale Operando Kinetic Decoupling of Photogenerated Carriers
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The energy-conversion efficiency of photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems is governed by photogenerated charge-carrier kinetics that span several orders of magnitude, from subpicosecond generation in the semiconductor bulk to millisecond consumption at catalytic surfaces. This vast temporal disparity severs the causal link between ultrafast carrier events and steady-state photocurrents, leaving the mechanistic origins of efficiency losses speculative and fundamentally hindering the rational optimization of PEC devices. Here, we bridge this gap by integrating multitime scale operando spectroscopies, ranging from transient absorption to electrochemical measurements, on model β-Fe2O3 photoanodes. This approach enables deconvolution of the temporal evolution of photogenerated carriers into distinct signatures attributable to bulk diffusion, charge accumulation, and catalytic-intermediate formation, thereby decoupling and identifying the dynamic fingerprints of carriers within a champion β-Fe2O3 photoanode. These fingerprints establish a mechanistic framework that directly connects multitime scale carrier dynamics and kinetics to the design principles of high-performance photoelectrodes, transforming the understanding of and approach to engineering solar water splitting systems.</jats:p>

Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Tailoring Spin-Crossover
Transitions in Fe(HB(tz)3)2 via Cocrystallization
for Low-Temperature Barocaloric
Cooling
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Spin-crossover (SCO) phase transitions can drive large barocaloric effects─thermal changes induced by applied hydrostatic pressure that enable heat to be moved against a temperature gradient. Although several SCO compounds have been reported to display promising barocaloric properties─including high pressure sensitivity, a large entropy change, and minimal transition hysteresis─it is challenging to control the transition temperature of a material without adversely impacting its phase-change behavior. This limitation restricts the scope of thermal applications relevant to a given SCO material. Here, we show how cocrystallization with solid coformers allows the SCO transition of Fe(HB(tz)3)2 (HB(tz)3– = hydrotris(1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)borate) to be manipulated across a wide temperature range. In particular, we report a series of cocrystals with SCO transition temperatures spanning from 185 to 350 K and varying degrees of associated hysteresis and cooperativity. We further establish structure–property relationships between coformer identity and SCO transition behavior through a combination of structural characterization, magnetometry, vibrational spectroscopy, and calorimetry. Notably, two cocrystals feature sharp SCO transitions near 200 K that produce large and highly reversible barocaloric effects in a low-temperature regime that has been difficult to access for most classes of barocaloric materials. More broadly, these results provide new insights into cocrystallization as a generalizable synthetic strategy for systematically tuning the properties of SCO materials.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Atomic
Layer Ordering of 2D van der Waals Ion Channels
Enables Ultrathin and Highly Selective Membranes
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Developing ultrathin, highly selective membranes that emulate biological ion channels is a primary goal of synthetic membrane technology. Although two-dimensional (2D) materials offer a promising platform for constructing subnanometer fluidic channels, simultaneously achieving high permeance and excellent selectivity in 2D ionic membranes remains a significant challenge. This bottleneck originates from the complexities involved in controlling the precise structural arrangement within nanosheet assemblies. In this work, we demonstrate that the atomic-layer ordering of 2D van der Waals (vdW) ion channels is a decisive factor in achieving ultrathin, highly selective membranes. By assembling 2D titania nanosheets with atomic layer-by-layer regularity, we fabricate atomic stacking membranes (ASMs) that achieve near-unity ion selectivity within an ultrathin (∼50 nm) framework. The structural regularity of these ASMs causes continuous overlap of the electrical double layer throughout the 2D ion channels, facilitating robust electrostatic regulation and maximizing selectivity. The result is further confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. Leveraging the “Lego-like” modular assembly advantage of ASMs, we demonstrate multifunctional heterostructural iontronic devices and gate-controlled iontronic transistors featuring on/off ratios up to 104. Furthermore, the well-ordered 2D ion channels within these ASMs enable high-performance osmotic energy harvesting. This solution-processable atomic-layer van der Waals assembly strategy for ultrathin and highly selective ASMs establishes a versatile platform for uniformly regulating 2D angstrom-scale ion transport, paving the way for advanced biomimetic iontronics and efficient energy conversion.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Macrocycle 2D COF Single
Crystal
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We report the synthesis of a two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic framework (COF) single crystal, termed COF-900, constructed from a geminiarene-type macrocycle linker, biphenyl-extended pillar[3]arene containing nine phenyl units. The atomically accurate structure was resolved by three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of the 2D COF single crystal with a resolution of 1.2 Å, unveiling the conformation of the macrocycle in the layered backbone as well as AB interlayer stacking. The macrocycle exhibits a similar stacking mode in both the COF and the molecular crystal of the linker, suggesting prealignment of linkers during COF crystal growth through a mechanism termed alignment-led framework assembly (ALFA). Cryo-transmission electron microscopy images further provided direct real-space visualization of the macrocycle, where three types of interconnected pores were clearly visualized with sizes of 1.1, 1.5, and 2.3 nm.</jats:p>

title:
Self-Induced Spin Glass
in Triangular-Lattice MnNCN
Stabilized by High-Pressure Synthesis
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The realization of spin glasses in the absence of structural disorder remains an enduring challenge in condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry. Geometrical frustration provides a route to disordered magnetism in long-range ordered crystals, yet canonical self-induced spin glass (SISG) beyond ultrapure rare-earth elements remains experimentally elusive. Here, we realize a metastable transition-metal SISG phase in MnNCN (R3̅m) via high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) synthesis, stabilizing a nonequilibrium state with enhanced magnetic competition. Magnetic measurements establish canonical spin-glass behavior, featuring a freezing temperature of 38.15 K and characteristic slowing-down dynamics, alongside a high coercivity of 1838 Oe. First-principles calculations reveal this SISG behavior is inherently rooted in the frustrated Mn triangular lattice. Mapping the energetic hierarchy uncovers strong competition among distinct antiferromagnetic superexchange pathways. Crucially, high-pressure-driven anisotropic lattice compression alters the Mn-ligand orbital overlap, significantly amplifying the intralayer coupling within the ab triangular planes. This chemical–mechanical modulation intensifies the competition between intralayer and dominant interlayer couplings, producing a strongly frustrated three-dimensional magnetic network. Energy evaluations verify a profound near-degeneracy among these competing states. Rapid quenching kinetically preserves this structurally ordered metastable phase, generating the complex energy landscape characteristic of a spin glass. Electronic-structure analyses further identify the Mn–N–C–N–Mn superexchange pathway mediated by covalent [N═C═N]2– ligands as the origin of magnetic coupling, yielding an intrinsic phase robustness surpassing fragile rare-earth SISGs. Magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) calculations suggest that the high coercivity mainly arises from extrinsic spin pinning associated with the nanograined microstructure, contributing to macroscopic anti-interference. Ultimately, the creation of the MnNCN SISG and the elucidation of its magnetic competition extend the SISG paradigm to transition-metal compounds, establishing HPHT synthesis as a targeted methodology for tailoring complex magnetism.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Single-Molecule Fluorescence
Imaging Reveals the Kinetic
Origin of Wettability-Controlled Photocatalytic Selectivity
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Interfacial wettability strongly influences photocatalytic selectivity, but the kinetic origin of this effect remains unclear. Although adsorption differences and dominant reactive oxygen species (ROS) pathways are often invoked to explain wettability-dependent selectivity, neither fully reveals how interfacial reaction environments determine catalytic outcomes. Here, we use single-molecule fluorescence imaging to directly resolve individual photocatalytic events on reversibly tunable hydrophilic and hydrophobic TiO2 interfaces that preferentially generate •OH- and 1O2-associated reaction environments, respectively. The results show that substrate adsorption remains largely comparable across different wettability states, whereas interfacial conversion kinetics constitute the dominant origin of the observed selectivity and product-release dynamics further amplify this effect. Combined with DFT calculations, the single-molecule analysis reveals the kinetic origin of wettability-controlled photocatalytic selectivity by correlating ROS-associated interfacial environments with interfacial reaction kinetics. This work establishes a single-molecule kinetic analysis framework for interrogating how interfacial microenvironments govern heterogeneous photocatalytic selectivity, providing an approach for linking interfacial regulation to catalytic kinetics and macroscopic outcomes.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Sequential Charge Transfer
via Synergistic Au Species
Boosts CO2 Photoreduction under Near-Infrared Irradiation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Photocatalytic CO2 reduction in the near-infrared (NIR) region suffers from low efficiency and poor selectivity, stemming from the energy mismatch between the low-energy nature of NIR photons and the high activation energy barrier of CO2 molecules. Moreover, it is challenging to achieve directed charge transfer, hindering the catalytic reaction kinetics. To overcome the bottleneck, we report a hybrid photocatalyst consisting of atomically dispersed Au single atoms (SAs) and Au nanoparticles (NPs) anchored on ultrathin CuCrP2S6 nanosheets (Aun/Au1–CCPS) for efficient NIR-driven CO2 photoreduction. Integrated crystal orbital Hamiltonian population (ICOHP) analysis reveals that orbital coupling among Au-5d, Cr-3d, and Cu-3d states in Aun/Au1–CCPS enhances the carbon affinity of Au species and facilitates CO2 activation by lowering the energy barrier for molecular orbital activation. Combined spectroscopic analyses and constrained density functional theory (CDFT-MIXED) calculations reveal that Au SAs regulate the electronic structure of CCPS and serve as electronic bridges connecting the CCPS substrate and neighboring Au NPs by strengthening interfacial electronic coupling. Additionally, an interfacial built-in electric field (BIEF) is induced, which significantly accelerates electron-transfer kinetics. Furthermore, adjacent Au SA sites cooperate with Au NPs to lower the formation energy barrier of the key *COOH intermediate, promoting CO evolution. As a consequence, the optimized Aun/Au1–CCPS catalyst exhibits exceptional CO generation activity of 96.08 μmol g–1 h–1 with nearly 100% selectivity, outperforming the majority of state-of-the-art catalysts in the NIR region. This study provides novel insights into the design of cooperative catalytic systems for high-efficiency photocatalytic CO2 conversion under NIR irradiation.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Sulfurization Breaking
the Ferroelectric Polarization
Bottleneck in PbTiO3
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Robust ferroelectricity is crucial for high-performance ferroelectric nonvolatile memories. PbTiO3 (PTO) is expected to show large polarization with a high Curie temperature (TC). However, the inherent leakage current of PTO limits its actual ferroelectricity. To address this limitation, we prepare PTO films via sulfurization using a cost-effective sol–gel method. The pristine PTO films show notable remnant polarization (Pr) of 61.6 μC/cm2 with well-saturated electric field–polarization loops that have not been achieved in either bulk or thin-film forms previously. Upon sulfurization, Pr increases to approximately 180% of its pristine value, rising from 61.6 to 111.7 μC/cm2 alongside a moderate coercive field of 697 kV/cm, rendering the films competitive among currently reported large polarization ferroelectrics (Pr &gt; 100 μC/cm2). Additionally, an elevated TC of up to 526 °C was observed in sulfurized PTO films, compared with 505 °C for pristine PTO thin films. First-principles calculations reveal that the sulfur-associated enhancement of tetragonal distortion substantially reduces the short-range restoring interaction, thereby shifting the balance between short-range and long-range forces toward a stronger polar instability; phase-field simulations further reproduce the enhanced ferroelectric polarization. Our study demonstrates an effective sulfurization method for achieving large ferroelectricity, holding great potential for ferroelectric devices.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Mechanisms
of Ammonia Synthesis over Ru Low- and High-Index
Surfaces Based on Density Functional Theory Calculations
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ammonia is a vital compound for the future, with significant potential in energy applications, such as hydrogen-powered vehicles, and in agriculture as a key ingredient in fertilizers essential for food production. Traditionally, ammonia has been synthesized via the Haber-Bosch process using an iron catalyst, which requires high temperatures (400 to 500 °C) and pressures (about 200 atm), leading to a substantial carbon footprint and energy costs. Ruthenium is a promising alternative catalyst due to its higher intrinsic catalytic activity, allowing for ammonia synthesis under milder conditions. This paper presents a detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) study of the elementary steps involved in ammonia production across five distinct facets: Ru(0001), Ru(10–10), Ru(11–20), Ru(11–21), and Ru(10–11). Using vibrational frequency analysis, we applied zero-point energy (ZPE), enthalpic, and entropic corrections at 80 °C. We also examined the competition with the hydrogen evolution reaction. Ultimately, we find that the step-edge coordination of the Ru(11–21) surface offers the most favorable thermodynamic pathway for NH3 formation and the most efficient catalytic performance. Nudged elastic band calculations on Ru(11–21) show that hydrogenation mediated by coadsorbed water has low barriers and that NH3 desorption is the most demanding step. Further, the Ru(11–21) surface favors water dissociation, while H2 evolution on the clean surface is uphill by 0.5 eV in free energy.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Revealing Bulk-Phase
Reactivity of Fe-Based Catalyst
in the Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Heterogeneous catalysis is conventionally interpreted as a surface-localized process, yet many catalysts undergo extensive reaction-driven restructuring that may fundamentally redistribute reactivity beyond the interface. Here we combine microscopy, isotope-labeling experiments, and large-scale molecular dynamics driven by a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP-MD) to investigate reactive carbon–oxygen chemistry in iron catalysts relevant to the reverse water–gas shift reaction. We show that under reaction conditions, the catalyst evolves into a dynamic FeOx/Fe3C mixed phase in which carbon and oxygen continuously redistribute across surface, subsurface and bulk regions. Isotope experiments reveal that bulk carbon is catalytically active, while simulations identify initial C–O association across a broad depth range, including within the catalyst interior, for carbon atoms subsequently removed as CO/CO2. Free-energy calculations characterize representative C–O association pathways at the surface and within the catalyst interior. Together, these results support CO formation beyond conventional surface sites and a surface-to-bulk catalytic picture for dynamically evolving iron catalysts.</jats:p>

title:
Vinylcyclopropanes
in Rearrangement Reactions
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Vinylcyclopropanes constitute highly versatile, strained building blocks whose unique reactivity has enabled the development of a broad variety of synthetically valuable rearrangement and cycloisomerization processes. Over more than six decades of development, vinylcyclopropane chemistry has undergone remarkable evolution, particularly in recent years. Accordingly, these transformations have emerged as powerful tools for the generation of molecular complexity through strain-release-driven reaction manifolds involving both homolytic and heterolytic bond-cleavage mechanistic pathways. This Review provides a comprehensive account of the current state of the art in vinylcyclopropane rearrangement chemistry, with particular emphasis on the mechanistic principles governing these transformations and on their synthetic applications in modern organic synthesis. The different rearrangement modes accessible to vinylcyclopropane derivatives are discussed, including stereomutation processes, vinylcyclopropane-cyclopentene rearrangements, divinylcyclopropane-cycloheptadiene rearrangements, vinylcyclopropane-to-skipped-1,4-diene rearrangements, and cycloisomerization reactions involving specifically functionalized vinylcyclopropane substrates. Particular attention is devoted to the influence of substrate structure, stereochemical features, catalyst design, and thermodynamic and kinetic factors on reaction outcome, in terms of efficiency and selectivity. The broad applicability of these transformations in the synthesis of structurally sophisticated carbo- and heterocyclic architectures, including natural-product-related targets, is highlighted together with current limitations and future opportunities for the continued development of vinylcyclopropane chemistry.</jats:p>
journal: Chemical Reviews

title: Synthetic Pathway Modulation of Metal Organization in Multivariate Metal–Organic Frameworks
content:
A synthetic strategy to modulate metal organization in multivariate metal–organic frameworks (MTV MOF) yield materials with nearly identical composition but distinct electronic, magnetic, and optical properties. By tuning the synthesis pathway, Co/Ni arrangements within 1D chains are modified, providing an additional synthetic variable for tuning framework properties.








ABSTRACT
Multivariate metal–organic frameworks (MTV MOFs) incorporate various metals and/or linkers within a periodic backbone, offering structural diversity and emergent functionalities. Typically, conventional one‐pot synthesis does not allow for any control over the spatial arrangement or sequencing of metals within the framework. Here, we present a synthetic strategy to alter metal arrangement in multimetallic MTV MOFs, yielding materials with nearly identical composition yet distinct properties. Using isostructural mCB‐Co and mCB‐Ni MOFs, we generate two MTV MOFs with different one‐dimensional Ni/Co arrangements, resulting in distinct semiconducting and magnetic properties. High‐resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI‐HRMS) reveals the formation of distinct precursor species in solution, suggesting that prenucleation chemistry influences the final metal arrangement. This work establishes a new approach for modulating metal arrangement in MTV MOFs, enabling tunable functional properties in multimetallic frameworks for applications in catalysis, electronics, and quantum materials.

title: Precise Control of Spin–Orbit Coupling for High‐Efficiency Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence: Toward Photo‐Responsive Patterning and Visual Oxygen Sensing
content:
A functional unit combination strategy tailors spin–orbit coupling (SOC) to reconcile the intrinsic trade‐off between high phosphorescence efficiency and oxygen sensitivity in pure organic room‐temperature phosphorescent materials. The resulting materials exhibit dynamic photo‐responsive behavior, enabling high‐contrast patterning for rewritable optical information storage with light writing and humidity erasure, as well as a simple, low‐cost visual oxygen sensing method.








ABSTRACT
Photo‐responsive pure organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials rely on the compatible synergy between high phosphorescence quantum yield (ΦP) and high oxygen sensitivity. However, a fundamental dilemma exists: high ΦP typically requires a shorter triplet exciton lifetime to suppress non‐radiative deactivation, whereas high oxygen sensitivity demands a longer triplet lifetime for efficient energy transfer. To resolve this contradiction, a series of pure organic RTP molecules are designed via the functional unit combination strategy. In these molecules, the flexible (4‐(tert‐butyl)phenyl)thio unit undergoes excited‐state geometric torsion, and the nonbonding n‐orbital of the sulfur atom is decoupled to varying degrees from the π‐orbital of the RTP core, enabling precise control of the spin‐orbit coupling (SOC) strength. Among them, the optimal molecule 56M2T achieves both a high oxygen sensitivity and a high ΦP of 87.6%, exhibiting excellent photo‐responsive RTP enhancement. Based on this photo‐responsive dynamic RTP, we have further developed a high‐contrast, cyclically‐stable “optical writing & humidity erasing” photo‐responsive patterning system and a low‐cost time‐dependent method for visual oxygen sensing. This work not only provides novel insights into the molecular design of highly efficient and oxygen‐sensitive RTP materials, but also sheds light on their application in the field of intelligent responses.

title: Self‐Confinement‑Tailored Energy Routing for Superior Thermal‐Adaptive Ln‐MOFs Scintillator
content:
A novel self‑confinement strategy is developed for constructing superior thermal‑adaptive Ln‑MOFs scintillators with enhanced exciton utilization, suppressed nonradiative energy dissipation, and optimized energy routing. Such inorganic‐organic hybrid materials with excellent scintillation performance enable high‐resolution radio‐imaging, remote radiation monitoring, and precise leakage localization, demonstrating significant potential in practical radiation safety and real‑time detection.








ABSTRACT
Noncontact radiation monitoring in extreme environments is essential across scientific and industrial fields, driving the development of x‑ray scintillators. Conventional scintillators continue to suffer from inadequate exciton utilization, poor thermal stability, or limited processability. In this study, we propose a self‐confinement strategy to tailor energy routing for constructing superior thermal‐adaptive scintillators. Two lanthanide‐organic frameworks, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln and Ln‐BDC‐F, are rationally designed and synthesized. Compared with the free state of pure ligand or its quasi‐confinement state in Ln‐BDC‐F, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln exhibits a strong molecular self‐confinement state arising from compact ligand packing, thereby enhancing exciton utilization, suppressing nonradiative energy dissipation, and optimizing the energy routing. These features endow ZJNU‐1006‐Ln with superior radio‐luminescent performance, including high light yield (max ∼ 62,000 photons MeV‒1), low detection limit (92.7 nGyair s‒1), and great thermal‐stability (< 7% emission intensity attenuation from 77 to 590 K). ZJNU‐1006‐Ln membranes and fibers demonstrate great potential for in situ, real‐time x‐ray imaging and radiation monitoring. In addition, by tracking radio‐luminescent chromaticity, a series of ZJNU‐1006‐Ln with varied Tb3+/Eu3+ doping ratios enables precise localization of radiation‐exposed regions over a broad temperature range, particularly encompassing the Earth surface temperature window. This work highlights the self‐confinement effect as a promising strategy for designing advanced inorganic‐organic scintillators.

title: An Interfacial Electron Pump Enhanced Photo‐Assisted CO2‐to‐Bioplastic Microbial Electrosynthesis
content:
Cell‐associated Ti3C2Tx MXene quantum dots (MQDs) form a conductive and photoactive interface that enhances lactate‐dependent extracellular electron transfer (EET) and adds an illumination‐dependent electron‐discharge contribution. Coupling this bioanode to an H2‐mediated Cupriavidus necator biocathode modified with Ni‐doped carbon dots and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (Ni‐CDs/PDDA) links upstream electron discharge to CO2 assimilation and polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) biosynthesis.








ABSTRACT
Most solar‐ and electrochemical CO2‐utilization strategies still terminate in small‐molecule products, whereas direct access to recoverable carbon products such as bioplastics remains uncommon. Here, we develop a photo‐assisted bioelectrochemical platform by coupling a Shewanella oneidensis MR‐1 bioanode functionalized with Ti3C2Tx MXene quantum dots (MQDs) to a Cupriavidus necator biocathode modified with Ni‐doped carbon dots/poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (Ni‐CDs/PDDA). Cell‐associated MQDs form a conductive and photoactive biointerface, operationally described as an interfacial electron pump, that facilitates lactate‐dependent extracellular electron transfer (EET) under applied anodic bias and adds an illumination‐dependent current contribution. The MQDs‐enabled microbial fuel cell (MFC) delivers a peak power density of 0.82 ± 0.03 mW cm−2 under illumination. In the coupled CO2‐fed system, anodic illumination raises polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) productivity to 131 mg L−1 d−1 at −0.6 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE), approximately 47% above the matched dark value over a 12 h interval. The coupled platform reaches an apparent total‐energy‐to‐PHB efficiency of 3.42% when electrical, incident optical, and lactate‐derived chemical inputs are included. Multiscale analyses support an EET‐coupled interfacial relay involving cytochrome/heme‐associated components within the native EET network. This interface‐to‐synthesis strategy links photo‐assisted microbial electron harvesting to H2‐mediated CO2‐to‐PHB biosynthesis.

title: Universal Thermally‐Driven Non‐Noble Metal Redistribution Strategy Boosts High‐Temperature CO2 Electrolysis
content:
A thermally‐induced redistribution strategy successfully achieves highly efficient redistribution of non‐noble metals from CeO2 to Sr2Fe1.5Mo0.5O6–δ (SFM) perovskite oxide surfaces during high‐temperature calcination. The redistributed Cu on the SFM surface markedly enhances CO2 reduction reaction activity, achieving a significantly superior leading electrolysis performance while simultaneously delivering excellent durability and adaptability across multiple operating scenarios.








ABSTRACT
Efficient and durable CO2 electrolysis in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) requires cathodes that integrate high activity with robust stability. Herein, a thermally‐driven non‐noble‐metal redistribution strategy is proposed to overcome the long‐standing limitation in dispersing non‐noble metals on perovskite surfaces, enabling perovskite–ceria composite cathodes with dynamically optimized active sites. Thermal treatment of Cu‐dispersed CeO2 (Cu0.05Ce0.95O2, 5CC) coupled with Sr2Fe1.5Mo0.5O6−δ (SFM) induces spontaneous Cu migration and redistribution, which can tailor the electronic structure, increase oxygen vacancies and extend triple‐phase boundaries, thereby enhancing CO2 adsorption, activation and O2−/e− transport. As a result, a single cell with 5CC–SFM cathode achieves exceptional current densities of 4.14 A cm−2 at 1.5 V under 850°C, respectively. Owing to strong interaction between the redistributed Cu species and perovskite oxide, the single cell maintains stable catalytic performance for 400 h under harsh high‐temperature CO2 electrolysis conditions. Moreover, this work demonstrates the extended applicability of 5CC–SFM cathode in reversible solid oxide cells (RSOCs) and establishes the generality and methodological significance of thermally‐driven redistribution in achieving highly dispersed non‐noble‐metal species on oxide supports. These findings offer a general framework for the rational design of next‐generation CeO2–containing SOEC cathodes and advanced composite materials.

title: Electrochemically Passivated Liquid Metal Printing for Two‐Dimensional Wafer‐Scale, Atomically‐Thin Non‐Layered Oxides
content:
Electrochemical passivation liquid metal printing, using an aluminum sacrificial anode, produces wafer‐scale atomically thin oxide films whose confined quantum states deliver exceptional photocatalysis, achieving 98.6% RhB degradation with a rate constant of 0.0355 min−1, alongside good cycling stability.








ABSTRACT
Two‐dimensional (2D) non‐layered metal oxides (NMOs) are promising for advanced electronics and catalysis owing to their tunable electronic structures and highly active surfaces. However, synthesizing wafer‐scale, atomically thin NMOs is challenging due to their intrinsic isotropic bonding. Here, we present an electrochemical passivation liquid metal printing strategy that regulates oxidation kinetics via galvanic coupling, enabling the synthesis of wafer‐scale, atomically thin NMOs in air. Critically, using aluminum foil as both a sacrificial anode and a high‐surface‐energy substrate enables a self‐limiting oxidation reaction and produces wafer‐scale and uniform α‐Bi2O3 films with thickness down to 0.7 nm when coupled with ultralow contact‐angle wetting (13.8°). This method demonstrates broad applicability, facilitating the synthesis of ultrathin films of various NMOs, including Ga2O3 (1 nm), In2O3 (1.5 nm), and ZnO (1.7 nm). Notably, the quantum confinement and abundant active sites in the 2D α‐Bi2O3 film enhance its light‐harvesting and promote charge separation, resulting in a photocatalytic degradation efficiency of 98.6% with a rate constant of 0.0355 min−1. This work provides a scalable strategy for synthesizing large‐area, ultrathin 2D NMOs, establishing a foundation for their applications in next‐generation photocatalysis.

title: Armoring Bubbles With Wettability‐Adaptive and Self‐Fusible Particles for Efficient Gas Handling in Air
content:
A time‐programmed wettability‐adaptive and self‐fusible particle modulates the gas marbles stability and their coalescence. Selected hydrophobic modification of adaptive particle programs wettability transition, enabling subsequent liquid adsorption, and self‐fusion. While, this transition drives capillary‐mediated coalescence of contacting gas marbles with minimal gas diffusion, a continuous gel layer forms because of self‐fusion of particles promotes long‐term storage of gas.








ABSTRACT
Mixing small quantities of gas and storing them in air is promising for developing a miniature gas reactor. Bubble encapsulation by liquid film has been considered; however, stabilizing the liquid layer while keeping bubble coalescence ability is challenging. Here, a time‐programmed wettability‐adaptive and self ‐ fusible particle is designed to modulate the coalescence ability and stability of gas bubbles. The adaptive particles remain initially hydrophobic and adsorb on the liquid layer surface, forming a stable gas‐barrier layer. After a modulated time of 10 to 600 s, the particles switch to hydrophilic and absorb available liquid. This adaptive wettability enables capillary‐driven automated coalescence of the contacting bubbles in air. After the preprogrammed time, the diffused particles self‐fuse and provide a continuous gel layer, allowing robust shell formation with tolerance to gas escape for at least 30 days. Proof of concept shows gas/gas and gas/liquid micro‐reactions and their long‐term storage.

title: Active Targeting Across Scales in Medical Robotics
content:
Medical robots can bridge the body's length scales by linking clinical access with controlled navigation and precise local action. This Review presents a cross‐scale access‐to‐action framework for active targeting and explains how anatomy, biological barriers, materials, actuation, and imaging shape application‐specific systems for diagnosis, therapy, and minimally invasive intervention, together with their paths toward clinical translation.








ABSTRACT
The diagnosis and treatment of human diseases often involve interventions that target different levels of the body's complex hierarchical organization, from macroscopic organs through microscopic cells, down to nanoscale molecular structures such as proteins. These interventions are hindered by challenges, such as biological barriers and dynamic microenvironments, which necessitate the development of more effective diagnosis, therapy, and microsurgery strategies. Multiscale medical robots are an emerging strategy to address these challenges: advances in micro and nano engineering have enabled the development of sophisticated medical robots with size adaptability and hierarchical navigation for active targeting. Such systems can connect organ‐level access and navigation with local action at tissue, cellular, or molecular scales. Here, we discuss advances in micro/nano engineering to design and fabricate multiscale medical robots, with focus on their active targeting capabilities in precision medicine. We provide an overview of the current state of these systems, from accurate diagnosis and targeted therapy to minimally invasive microsurgery across the various scales of the human body, and explore how anatomical, biological, and imaging constraints shape their design. Finally, we discuss the practical challenges of clinical translation, including system‐level assessment within the intended clinical workflow and the need for collaboration between engineers and clinicians.

title: One Acceptor Core, Two Bright Pathways: CF3‐Substituted Triazines Achieve Highly Efficient Intermolecular Exciplexes and Intramolecular TADF
content:
A CF3‐substituted triazine (T4) scaffold provides a unified platform for efficient thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) through both inter‐ and intramolecular charge‐transfer (CT) processes. Intermolecular CT‐based exciplexes achieve record‐high emission efficiency, while T4‐3Cz exhibits strong three‐photon absorption (3PA) and high photostability, highlighting multifunctional potential in optoelectronic and bioimaging applications.








ABSTRACT
Intermolecular charge‐transfer (CT)‐based exciplexes provide broad design flexibility through independent donor and acceptor selection, but often suffer from low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) due to limited orbital overlap. In contrast, intramolecular CT‐based thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) systems can achieve high PLQYs through controlled donor‐acceptor interactions, but generally require precise molecular design and substituent tuning. Here, we show that a CF3‐substituted triazine scaffold (T4) serves as a unified molecular platform for achieving highly efficient emission through both intermolecular and intramolecular CT pathways. The CzCF3‐substituted derivatives T4‐2CzCF3 and T4‐3CzCF3 formed highly emissive intermolecular exciplexes with mCBP, achieving PLQYs of 100%. Incorporation of stronger carbazole donors afforded T4‐3Cz, which exhibited intramolecular CT‐based TADF with PLQYs reaching 100% in solution and 100% in an mCBP‐doped film. T4‐3Cz also displayed near‐infrared multiphoton absorption, with a two‐photon absorption cross‐section (σ2) of 80 GM at 780 nm and a three‐photon absorption cross‐section (σ3) of 2.94 × 10−80 cm6 s2 at 1210 nm. Furthermore, OLEDs based on the T4‐3CzCF3 intermolecular exciplex and the intramolecular CT‐based TADF emitter T4‐3Cz exhibited efficient electroluminescent performance. These findings establish the T4 scaffold as a versatile molecular framework that integrates highly efficient intermolecular exciplex TADF, intramolecular CT‐based TADF, multiphoton absorption, and OLED functionality.

title: Mitochondria‐Inspired COF Nanochannels for Reversible Directional Ion Transport for Osmotic Power Generation
content:
Inspired by mitochondrial ATP synthase, pH‐responsive COF nanochannel membranes achieve adaptive, directional ion transport without permanent asymmetry. Transmembrane pH polarization induces asymmetric charge regulation and internal electric fields, yielding ionic conductance from 0.4 to ∼1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Under a 100‐fold NaCl gradient, these membranes deliver 20.2 W m−2.








ABSTRACT
Directional ion transport in artificial nanochannels usually relies on fixed structural or chemical asymmetry, which restricts adaptive regulation. Inspired by proton transport in mitochondrial ATP synthase, we fabricate pH‐responsive PAN‐supported COF nanochannel membranes via liquid–liquid confined interfacial polymerization. Transmembrane pH polarization triggers asymmetric charge regulation and builds an internal electric field. The membranes show pH‐dependent ion transport, with conductance spanning 0.4–1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Under a 100‐fold NaCl gradient and pH 1/13 polarization, they deliver 20.2 W m−2. Experiments verify pH‐dependent COF charge regulation, while simulations indicate internal electric fields modulate ion migration together with diffusion. Salinity and pH gradients supply transport driving force; COF charge regulation dominates directional transport, and electrolyte properties, ion mobilities and electrochemical potentials tune current and output power. The observation of analogous directional transport across six chemically distinct membrane systems suggests the broader applicability of pH‐mediated transport regulation. These results provide insight into adaptive ion regulation and a strategy for energy conversion under combined salinity and pH gradients.

title: Promoting CO2 Electromethanation via Reverse H‐Spillover on Zeolite Y‐Confined CuO Nanoclusters
content:
Conventional CuO exhibits distributed product selectivity during electrocatalytic CO2 reduction, while the encapsulation of CuO within the zeolite Y framework promotes the sequential hydrogenation of key intermediate *CO via reverse hydrogen spillover, thereby achieving a methane Faradaic efficiency exceeding 70% and a maximum partial current density of 656.1 mA cm−2.








ABSTRACT
The electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (eCO2RR) presents a promising route for converting CO2 emissions into valuable products, with methane (CH4) being particularly attractive owing to its high energy density and infrastructure compatibility. However, selective CH4 formation via sequential *CO hydrogenation remains kinetically challenged by competing C–C coupling pathways. Here, we encapsulate CuO nanoclusters within zeolite Y, where spatial confinement enables the uniform dispersion of CuO and enhances the reverse H‐spillover (RHS)‐mediated utilization of *H species generated on the zeolite support for sequential *CO hydrogenation. The optimized catalyst achieves a CH4 Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% ± 1.3% at 600 mA cm−2 and 65.6% ± 1.0% at 1000 mA cm−2. Experimental and theoretical studies show that H2O is preferentially activated on the zeolite support, generating *H species that are rapidly transferred to adjacent CuO via RHS for CO2 hydrogenation. Operando spectroscopic detection of CH4‐related *OCH3/*CHx intermediates, together with DFT calculations, indicates that zeolite–CuO interactions favor *CO hydrogenation to *CHO over *CO dimerization, thereby promoting CH4 formation. This work establishes spatial confinement‐coupled RHS as an effective strategy for regulating interfacial *H transfer and sequential hydrogenation in the eCO2RR process.

title: Rationale‐Guided and Iterative Learning for Redesigning a Highly Enantio‐ and Chemoselective Flavin‐Dependent Phenolic Hydroxylase
content:
Engineering biocatalysts for precise enantio‐ or chemoselectivity typically demands exhaustive effort, owing to the large number of screening iterations and the reliance on reliable mutational analysis. Here, we introduce a mechanistic insight‐guided iterative learning workflow capable of simultaneously redesigning catalytic preferences of a flavin‐dependent monooxygenase—achieved within just three rounds of single or double saturation mutagenesis per round.








ABSTRACT
Flavin‐dependent monooxygenases (FDMOs) can catalyze C─H hydroxylation of phenolic compounds, yet the scope of their application has never been challenged beyond the hydroxylation of simple substrates nor explored for the ability to achieve selective hydroxylation. FDMO hydroxylation is often poorly controlled, yielding unstable, multiply hydroxylated products. Here, we used a mechanistic insight‐guided iterative learning workflow to redesign the active site of p‐hydroxyphenylacetate hydroxylase to expand its capability for chemo‐ and enantioselective control in the synthesis of (R)‐norepinephrine. Within only three rounds of an engineering campaign, a DISD_LG variant that switched from (S)‐ to (R)‐selective hydroxylation was obtained with excellent enantioselectivity (97.6%ee (R)). This variant also produced markedly fewer multiply hydroxylated products (<5% relative amount in the product mixture), indicating significant improvement in chemoselective control. The kinetic resolution was performed at a 20‐mL scale (4 mM racemic substrate) and (R)‐norepinephrine was obtained with 48.8% isolated yield and 96.2%ee (R). The molecular mechanisms underlying the enantio‐ and chemoselective control achieved by the DISD_LG variant were elucidated using molecular dynamics simulations. This work presents an enzyme engineering workflow to achieve kinetic resolution in combination with a controllable degree of hydroxylation, the aspects previously overlooked or underemphasized in FDMOs.

title: Pronounced Visible‐Light Cryptochirality Detection of Various Terpenoids via Helical Polyaromatic Capsules
content:
The efficient CD analysis of cryptochiral terpenoids is demonstrated by helical polyaromatic capsules upon simple encapsulation in water. The resultant host‐guest complexes exhibit intense CD bands in the visible region (|Δε| up to ∼130 M−1 cm−1) derived from guest‐induced host helicity. The use of two different capsules enables the chirality detection of diverse mono‐, sesqui‐, di‐, and triterpenoids in the same way.








ABSTRACT
Cryptochirality refers to molecular chirality with undetectable/absent circular dichroism (CD) bands. Whereas there have been several host compounds capable of binding cryptochiral biosubstrates for their analysis, those with guest‐induced CD activity in the visible region remain quite rare so far. We herein report the host‐guest interaction‐based CD analysis of various terpenoids using two different, helical polyaromatic capsules under ambient aqueous conditions. When one molecule of CD‐inactive monoterpenoid, (–)‐carvone, is quantitatively encapsulated within a CD‐inactive capsule bearing a spheroidal cavity, the resultant host‐guest complex displays pronounced CD bands in the range of 350–430 nm with a relatively high absolute molar circular dichroism value (i.e., |Δε| >80 M−1cm−1 at ∼390 nm), derived from the guest‐induced host helicity. The chirality of other cryptochiral mono/sesquiterpenoids is also detected with similar efficiency (∼30–90 M−1cm−1). The enantiomeric excess (%ee) of d/l‐mixtures of monoterpenoids can be determined with the helical cavity via comparative CD analysis. By the use of another larger capsule, di‐ and triterpenoids also induce its intense CD bands (up to ∼130 M−1cm−1) in the visible region upon encapsulation. The present study highlights the potential application of helical polyaromatic hosts to the facile cryptochiral analysis of a broad range of biosubstrates with intense CD output.

title: Topological Regioisomerism Enables Triplet–Triplet Energy‐Transfer for Reversible Dual Delayed Fluorescence–Phosphorescence Multicolor Afterglow
content:
Regioisomer‐controlled host‐guest engineering enables triplet‐triplet energy transfer‐driven dual delayed fluorescence‐phosphorescence afterglow with fully reversible, temperature‐dependent color switching (yellow → orange → red) from room temperature to cryogenic conditions.








ABSTRACT
Achieving concurrent thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) afterglow in purely organic systems remains elusive owing to limited control over triplet dynamics, competing decay pathways and unclear operational mechanisms. Reversible TADF/RTP modulation within a single host‐guest system is challenging, hindering advances in color‐ and lifetime‐tunable afterglow materials. To achieve this, we utilized regioisomerism as a structural topology control parameter in a host‐guest platform to modulate triplet‐triplet energy transfer (TTET), enabling the transition from exciplex TADF to dual TADF‐RTP afterglow. The optimized system exhibits TADF‐associated delayed emission with an intensity‐weighted apparent lifetime of 617 ms, along with persistent RTP and ∼6.5‐9.5 s afterglow. Temperature‐dependent modulation of ITADF/IRTP ratio enables reversible cryogenic afterglow color evolution from yellow to orange and red through thermally regulated exciton redistribution.

title: Irradiation‐Wavelength‐Tuned Stepwise [2+2] Cycloaddition of Indolylphenylpropenone Derivatives as a Platform for Light–Mechanical Energy Conversion
content:
Indolylphenylpropenone derivatives can be transformed into monocyclobutane and bicyclobutane products by tuning the irradiation wavelength. Blue light induces the formation of monocyclobutane via [2+2] cycloaddition of the vinyl groups, accompanied by a single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal transformation, while UV light activates the dearomatization of indole to afford bicyclobutane. Driven by photocycloaddition, the molecular crystals exhibit pronounced photomechanical effects.








ABSTRACT
Cyclobutane motifs are widely present in natural products, and [2+2] cycloaddition provides a facile route for synthesizing four‐membered rings. However, controlling the regio‐ and stereo‐selectivity of cycloaddition remains a great challenge. In topo‐photochemical reaction, the prearrangement of the reactant molecules can place the atoms at specific positions in the products. In this work, irradiation‐wavelength‐controlled, stepwise photo‐induced topo‐[2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives was achieved in crystals. Under blue light, one kind of monocyclobutane was produced via the cycloaddition of the vinyl groups; for (E)‐1‐(5‐bromo‐1H‐indol‐1‐yl)‐3‐(3,5‐difluorophenyl)prop‐2‐en‐1‐one (PEOBr5F35), this process proceeded via a single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal transformation. Upon subsequent irradiation with 365 nm light, the monocyclobutane product underwent a second‐step [2+2] cycloaddition between C = C bonds on five‐membered heterocyclic ring in indole, converting into a bicyclobutane product. Such catalyst‐free dearomatization of indole via [2+2] cycloaddition provide a facile and green strategy for constructing cyclobutane‐fused heterocyclic architectures. Driven by [2+2] cycloaddition, the molecular crystals exhibited obvious macroscopic mechanical motion.

title: A Scalable Presodiation Strategy Enabling Dry‐Air‐Processable Hard Carbon Anodes for High Energy Sodium‐Ion Batteries
content:
Synchronized acoustic and interfacial engineering enable rapid, homogeneous sodium compensation in thick hard carbon electrodes for a dry‐air‐processable manufacturing of high energy sodium‐ion batteries.








ABSTRACT
Hard carbon (HC) anodes hold promise for sodium‐ion batteries but are plagued by low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) stemming from irreversible sodium sequestration. Chemical presodiation offers a direct route to compensate this deficit, yet its translation to high‐loading electrodes is crippled by sluggish mass transport and air sensitivity of the sodiated product, a barrier to scalable manufacturing. Here, we break this impasse by synchronizing acoustic field enhanced transport with in situ interfacial engineering. Ultrasound‐driven microconvection and cavitation overcome diffusion limitations within thick electrodes, delivering ∼100% ICE within one minute, approximately twice as fast as conventional immersion. A five second quenching in sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate constructs a B/F‐rich hybrid interphase that not only passivates the highly reactive sodiated surface against dry‐air degradation, retaining >79% ICE after 6 h exposure, but also selfregulates subsequent solid‐electrolyte interphase evolution, suppressing impedance growth and stabilizing charge transfer kinetics. Practical pouch cells deliver 76% capacity retention over 700 cycles at 0.5 C/1 C and exhibit superior wide‐temperature adaptability from −40°C to 55°C. By resolving the coupled bottlenecks of kinetic inhomogeneity and environmental instability, this work establishes a scalable, dry‐air‐compatible presodiation paradigm that bridges the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial battery manufacturing.

title: Photocatalytic 1,2‐Boron Migrative Alkene Homologation to Access 1,3‐Difunctionalized Alkenes
content:
A visible light photocatalytic 1,2‐boron migrative alkene homologation is achieved with tert‐butylsulfonyl alkyl halides as a new type of vinylidene donors, producing structurally diverse remotely functionalized alkenes under mild conditions.








ABSTRACT
In contrast to well‐established methods for vicinal di‐functionalization of alkenes, remote di‐functionalization is much more challenging and has achieved limited success. Herein, we disclose a visible light photocatalytic boron‐directed alkene homologation with alkyl halides activated by a traceless tert‐butylsulfonyl (Bus) leaving group. The reaction produces a myriad of 1,3‐difunctionalized alkenes under mild conditions with excellent functional group tolerance. β‐Elimination of the Bus group not only drives the contra‐thermodynamic 1,2‐boron migration, but also regenerates a C─C double bond, thus transforming the sulfone‐based alkyl halide into a vinylidene precursor, rather than a traditional alkyl source. The synthetic utility of this method is well demonstrated by gram‐scale synthesis, downstream transformations, and the formal total synthesis of 24‐fluoro‐25‐hydroxyvitamin D3 analogues. This work represents a very rare example of one‐carbon homologation of ubiquitous alkenes, thus establishing a new strategic paradigm for chemical synthesis.

title: Reconfiguring Interfacial Electrochemical Potential for Boosting Sodium‐Ion Transport in Composite Solid Electrolytes
content:
Interfacial electrochemical potential is modulated through descriptor‐guided molecular grafting to facilitate sodium‐ion transport in composite solid electrolytes (CSEs). Phenyltrimethoxysilane reduces the KPFM‐derived surface potential mismatch by 87% and suppresses interfacial sodium‐ion depletion. Lower interfacial migration barriers accompany these changes. The modified electrolyte exhibits enhanced ionic conductivity and enables stable cycling in all‐solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries.








ABSTRACT
Sluggish ion transport kinetics between the ceramic and polymer phases remain a key challenge in composite solid electrolytes (CSEs), primarily due to a severe interfacial barrier arising from their intrinsic physicochemical incompatibility. Herein, molecular design‐enabled electronic structure engineering is proposed to reconfigure the interfacial electrochemical environment at the Na3Zr2Si2PO12–poly(ethylene oxide) interface, based on a dual‐axis screening guided by the electron‐donating capability and molecular electronic asymmetry. By grafting different functional trimethoxysilanes from a targeted library onto the ceramic surface, the effect of the interfacial electrochemical potential on Na‐ion transport is investigated, revealing a strong negative correlation with the ionic conductivity of CSEs. The CSE with the optimal grafting molecule (phenyltrimethoxysilane) reduces the potential mismatch by 87% and lowers the Na‐ion migration barrier, thereby boosting Na‐ion conductivity by two orders of magnitude. All‐solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries using this CSE show boosted electrochemical performance with a high capacity of 91.8 mAh g−1 delivered at 5 C and retain ∼99% of their initial capacity after 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes a screening framework for reducing interfacial potential mismatch and addressing the long‐standing ion‐transport bottleneck across ceramic–polymer interfaces in CSEs.

title: Engineering Amino‐Induced p‐π Conjugation for Electronic Regulation of Li+ Transport in PVDF‐Based Solid‐State Electrolytes
content:
Amino‐functionalized UiO66‐NH2 triggers p‐π conjugation and strengthened LMCT, weakening Li+‐FSI− pairing to accelerate Li+ migration. The composite SPE achieves good electrochemical performance and stable cycling for high‐loading solid‐state lithium metal batteries. 








ABSTRACT
Sluggish Li+ transport in poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)‐based solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) arises from restricted polymer segmental motion and persistent Li+‐FSI− association, while conventional fillers provide limited regulation of the local electronic and coordination environments. Herein, amino‐functionalized UiO66‐NH2 is introduced into a PVDF/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) electrolyte to construct electronically active composite SPEs (U6NP). The electron‐donating ─NH2 groups induce p‐π conjugation, redistribute the linker electron density, and strengthen ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT)‐related electronic coupling between the organic linkers and Zr‐O clusters. This electronic reconstruction, together with amino‐associated modulation of local O‐centered coordination environments, reshapes the electrostatic landscape, weakens Li+‐FSI− interactions, and facilitates Li+ migration. U6NP delivers a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 2.41 × 10−3 S cm−1, a Li+ transference number of 0.56, and an oxidative stability of 4.42 V. More importantly, Li||U6NP||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) cells with a cathode loading of 21.5 mg cm−2 retain 98.51% after 120 cycles at 0.05 C. The Li||U6NP||NCM811 pouch cell delivers 136.6 mAh g−1 initially and 120.9 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles. This work establishes ─NH2‐induced p‐π conjugation‐enhanced LMCT as an effective strategy for electronically active MOF‐reinforced PVDF electrolytes toward high‐loading solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

This work provides a new paradigm for the designed synthesis of high‐performance ultraviolet nonlinear optical materials.

title: Ag─S Sites Steer Furfural Electroreduction to Furfuryl Alcohol
content:
A simple sulfide incorporation strategy turns silver into a highly active and selective catalyst for furfural electroreduction to furfuryl alcohol. Experiments combined with density functional theory reveal how isolated S sites promote hydrogenation while suppressing hydrofuroin coupling, enabling selective biomass upgrading.








ABSTRACT
The electrochemical upgrading of furfural (FF), a biomass‐derived platform molecule, using renewable electricity offers a promising route toward green and sustainable chemical synthesis. However, achieving high selectivity toward hydrogenated products, such as furfuryl alcohol (FA), remains challenging as hydrogenation competes with C─C coupling reactions that generate undesired dimers. In this study, we show that trace sulfide species introduced into the electrolyte dynamically generate Ag─S sites on Ag surfaces during electrolysis, thereby steering the FF reduction reaction toward FA formation. Using Ag disk electrodes, the introduction of 0.5 mM sulfide ions (S2−) into the electrolyte increases the Faradaic efficiency (FE) for FA formation from 59% to 88% and enhances its partial current density (jFA) from 5.4 to 12.5 mA cm−2. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, in situ Raman spectroscopy, and density functional theory simulations collectively reveal that the low‐coverage sulfide species on Ag regulate FF adsorption and facilitate proton transfer to the carbonyl oxygen, steering FA formation, while suppressing hydrofuroin (HF) formation by disrupting the Ag ensembles required for C─C coupling. Overall, our findings establish the deliberate introduction of trace sulfide into the electrolyte as a simple and potentially broadly applicable strategy to steer selectivity in the electrochemical hydrogenation of biomass‐derived furanic aldehydes.

title: Enhanced Hydrogen Evolution Activity of MoS2 Through Solid Solution Modification of Its Edge Sites With Ruthenium
content:
Modulating the edge sites of molybdenum disulfide significantly boosts hydrogen production. By depositing Ru to form an edge‐coordinated solid solution, we accelerate water dissociation and shift the hydrogen evolution reaction pathway to Volmer–Tafel. This design achieves ampere‐level current densities and outstanding stability, offering a robust strategy for renewable fuel generation. 








ABSTRACT
In hydrogen production, electrocatalysts featuring edge sites as active centers, modulation of its edge site coordination environment could greatly improve the reaction kinetics by effectively reducing the energy barrier. Here, we report a novel catalyst formulation obtained by the electrochemical deposition of ruthenium onto the edge sites and near‐edge basal plane of MoS2 to yield Ru‐coordinated solid solution species. The Ru atom acts as a site for water dissociation, increasing the proton supply rate and, in turn, the catalytic activity of MoS2. Based on the Tafel slope, in situ Raman, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) analysis, the edge solid solution creates a locally acidic chemical environment, enhancing the kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction by altering the reaction pathway from Volmer–Heyrovsky observed for pristine MoS2 to Volmer–Tafel. Edge‐coordinated Ru solid solution catalyst features a very high current density in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) and demonstrates excellent long‐term stability when compared with other reported MoS2‐ and Ru‐based catalysts. Overall, our studies demonstrate that modification of MoS2 by the incorporation of an edge solid solution can markedly improve its catalytic activity and, therefore, represents a promising strategy for materials design in the field of renewable fuel generation.

title: Controlled Presodiation of Sodium‐Ion Cathode via Electron Cloud Engineering
content:
This study introduces a novel electron cloud engineering strategy for mild chemical presodiation in sodium‐ion batteries. By modifying π‐conjugated systems with electron‐withdrawing groups, 1‐indanone treatment enhances Na0.44MnO2 cathode performance. This work offers a promising route for high‐performance sodium‐ion batteries.








ABSTRACT
Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium‐ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2‐ and tunnel‐type cathodes, such as Na0.44MnO2, where the as‐synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron‐cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π‐conjugation size and introducing electron‐withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1‐indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na0.44MnO2 cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first‐cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.

title: A Locally Flexible Kinetic Valve for Temperature‐Programmed Guest Release and Hydrogen Isotope Separation in Metal–Organic Frameworks
content:
Locally flexible gates in C5‐IRMOF act as a kinetic valve, trapping guests in a confined cavity and reopening only at elevated temperature. Increasing the exposure temperature shifts the guest‐release maximum to higher desorption temperatures, establishing adsorption‐temperature‐programmed desorption as a distinct pore function.








ABSTRACT
Controlling when an adsorbed guest leaves a porous solid is as important as controlling how much it takes up, yet desorption is almost always dictated by adsorption‐site energetics and the heating profile, leaving little room to program the release temperature. Here, we show that a locally flexible pore aperture can act as a kinetic valve that converts the temperature at which a guest is loaded into the temperature at which it is later released. In a pentoxy‐functionalized isoreticular MOF (C5‐IRMOF), long alkoxy side chains line the aperture to form a strongly confined, thermally responsive gate while preserving a large internal cavity. Unlike its butoxy analogue (C4‐IRMOF), a conventional microporous adsorbent, C5‐IRMOF traps guests until thermally activated chain motions reopen the gate, releasing them abruptly at an unusually high temperature without any strong binding sites. Cryogenic thermal desorption spectroscopy reveals that the release maximum shifts with a near‐unity slope with respect to the initial exposure temperature, defining adsorption‐temperature‐programmed desorption as a distinct mode of pore function, while the same confinement enables kinetic quantum sieving of hydrogen isotopes up to 100 K. These results establish locally flexible side chains as a simple design handle for programming guest release in porous materials.

title: Light‐Driven Control of Polar Order in Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystals
content:
Light‐responsive ferroelectric nematics are achieved by molecularly matching azobenzene photo‐switches to the polar packing motif of DIO. This design yields intrinsically photo‐responsive ferroelectric nematic mesogens and optically addressable DIO blends, in which light reversibly modulates spontaneous polarization and switches between high‐ and low‐permittivity states. 








ABSTRACT
Ferroelectric nematic (NF) liquid crystals are polar fluids that combine long‐range orientational order with spontaneous macroscopic polarization and exceptionally large dielectric permittivity. While these properties make NF materials attractive for responsive soft devices, incorporating additional functionality remains challenging because polar order is highly sensitive to molecular mismatch. Here we introduce a molecular design strategy that enables optical control of NF materials using azobenzene‐based mesogens structurally matched to the archetypal NF compound DIO. Two derivatives are themselves ferroelectric nematogens, demonstrating that photoisomerizable mesogens can intrinsically sustain and modulate NF polar order, with large and reversible light‐induced changes in polarization and dielectric permittivity. The same structural matching principle also enables non‐NF azobenzenes to co‐assemble with DIO at concentrations up to 20 wt.% while preserving ferroelectric nematic order. In selected blends, light irradiation drives a reversible transition from the ferroelectric nematic state to a low‐permittivity state consistent with antiferroelectric smectic order. Together, light and temperature provide complementary handles to navigate this phase landscape of competing ferroelectric and antiferroelectric order. These results provide a molecular design strategy for programming collective polar order in ferroelectric nematic fluids using light‐responsive mesogens.

title: Inducing Radicality in Gold‐Coordinated Porphyrinoids Through Precise Tip‐Induced Covalent Bond Dissociation
content:
STM imaging and schematic representation of tip‐induced controlled bond scission of carbonitrile─Au ligands in a π‐extended porphyrinoid, switching the molecule from a closed‐shell to an open‐shell configuration.








ABSTRACT
π‐Extended porphyrinoids are versatile platforms for the emerging field of π‐electron magnetism in conjugated systems. However, achieving controlled bond‐selective transformations that enable tuning of their electronic ground states remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a protocol for covalent bond dissociation in π‐extended porphyrinoids at carbonitrile‐Au substituents. By applying bias pulses with an STM tip positioned close to the molecule, the ligand can be selectively cleaved, resulting in chemisorption of the porphyrinoid onto the Au(111) surface. BR‐STM provides structural insights into the bonding configurations before and after the scission, while STS in combination with DFT+CASCI calculations reveals the impact of the cleavage on the molecule's electronic properties. Whereas the intact molecule exhibits a closed‐shell electronic structure, removal of the ligands induces a change in its electronic ground state, leading to the emergence of a Kondo resonance upon cleavage of the CN─Au ligands. In addition, DFT + vdW simulations show that carbonitrile─Au coordination weakens the carbon─carbon bond connecting the ligand to the molecular core, thereby facilitating its cleavage through tip‐induced manipulation. Overall, these results provide insights into the bonding nature of the carbonitrile─Au interaction and demonstrate how the bond scission induces a transition from closed‐shell to open‐shell states.

title: Supramolecular Pretargeting Lipid Nanoparticles Based on Host–Guest Recognition Potentiate Cancer Immunotherapy by Reprogramming Tumor Microenvironment
content:
This supramolecular pretargeting strategy exploiting ultrahigh‐affinity CB[7]–ADA recognition enables enhanced tumor accumulation of engineered lipid nanoparticles (CN‐LNPs). Combined with IDO1 inhibition and circular RNA‐encoding interleukin‐2 cytokine, this integrated platform reprograms the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and stimulates the antitumor immune responses.








ABSTRACT
Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as a promising platform for gene/drug delivery in cancer therapy, however their nonspecific biodistribution and extensive hepatosplenic sequestration result in insufficient intratumoral accumulation, thereby undermining the therapeutic efficacy. Here, we establish a sequential pretargeting strategy exploiting the high‐affinity host–guest recognition between adamantane (ADA) and cucurbit[7]uril (CB[7]) to enhance tumor enrichment. Preadministered ADA‐conjugated anti‐PD‐L1 antibody (ADA‐αPD‐L1) primes tumors for efficient capture of subsequently infused CB[7]‐functionalized LNPs (CN‐LNPs), improving intratumoral retention and cellular uptake. To concurrently address the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, NLG919 is covalently incorporated into the ionizable lipid of CN‐LNPs to inhibit IDO‐mediated tryptophan catabolism, effectively attenuating regulatory T cell activity while preserving the pretargeting functionality of the nanocarrier. CN‐LNPs are employed as a delivery platform to encapsulate a circular RNA encoding IL‐2‐Fc fusion protein (CN‐LNPs@cRNAIL‐2F), enabling intratumoral cytokine production to potentiate antitumor immunity. CN‐LNPs@cRNAIL‐2F elicit robust antitumor immunity to suppress tumor growth and extend survival, establishing a versatile platform that overcomes the intratumoral delivery limitations commonly associated with conventional LNPs system.

title: Enhancing Stability of Layered Double Perovskites With a Naphthalene Diimide Spacer Toward Photoelectrochemical Application
content:
A bulky, hydrophobic naphthalene diimide dication spacer (NDI‐dH2+) endows the lead‐free layered double perovskite (NDI‐dH)2AgBiI8 with threefold‐higher in‐plane carrier mobility, an order‐of‐magnitude lower trap density, and exceptional water tolerance compared to aliphatic and benzene‐based analogues, enabling the first sustained photoelectrochemical operation of a layered hybrid double perovskite photoanode in aqueous electrolyte.








ABSTRACT
Lead‐free layered hybrid double perovskites (LHDPs) promise stable, non‐toxic optoelectronic devices, but operating these materials in applications with a direct semiconductor/water interface remains a challenge. We show that a bulky, hydrophobic naphthalene diimide dication spacer (NDI‐dH2+) in (NDI‐dH)2AgBiI8 yields threefold‐higher in‐plane carrier mobility and an order‐of‐magnitude lower trap density than analogous aliphatic or aromatic spacers, together with exceptional tolerance to humidity and liquid water. This enables the first photoelectrochemical operation of an LHDP in aqueous electrolyte (producing 0.25 mA cm−2 at +1.0 V vs RHE under 1‐sun illumination), sustained beyond 1 h with a hole‐transporting overlayer. Notably, light harvested by the organic spacer contributes productively to photocurrent, despite a type‐I nanoheterojunction. Overall, this work establishes key routes of spacer engineering for robust lead‐free LHDPs.

title: Phosphate‐Modulated Asymmetric Copper Catalysis for Photochemical Enantioselective S‐Benzylation of Sulfenamides
content:
A visible‐light‐driven copper/PyOx/phosphate catalytic platform enables asymmetric radical benzylation of sulfenamides via three distinct radical‐generation pathways, delivering enantioenriched S‐stereogenic sulfilimines under mild conditions. The bulky phosphate anion acts as a multifunctional secondary‐sphere regulator that modulates the copper coordination environment and stabilizes key intermediates, collectively ensuring high reactivity and enantioselectivity.








ABSTRACT
S‐stereogenic sulfilimines constitute valuable S(IV)‐based scaffolds widely encountered in chiral ligands, pharmaceuticals, and bioactive molecules, yet their catalytic enantioselective construction remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a versatile copper catalytic platform assembled from a chiral pyridine‐oxazoline (PyOx) ligand, a bulky phosphate, and a Cu(I) salt to generate the active catalyst. This chiral copper/PyOx/phosphate system accommodates three mechanistically distinct radical‐generation pathways upon light irradiation, encompassing single‐electron transfer reduction of Katritzky salts, proton‐coupled electron transfer decarboxylation of carboxylic acids, and hydrogen atom transfer activation of toluene derivatives. Such flexibility enables efficient asymmetric radical benzylation of readily accessible sulfenamides under mild conditions. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the phosphate anion serves a multifunctional role, modulating the copper coordination sphere and stabilizing key copper–sulfur intermediates, which collectively boost both reactivity and enantioselectivity. The methodology delivers enantioenriched sulfilimines with broad substrate scope and operational simplicity. This work establishes a general blueprint for integrating multiple radical‐generation modes into a single stereocontrolled catalytic framework, demonstrating that rational modulation of the secondary coordination sphere can unlock new possibilities in stereoselective radical chemistry.

title: Highly Stabilized and Accessible Sub‐Nanometer RuBi Heteroclusters Drive Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
content:
Sterically stabilized and highly accessible sub‐nanometer RuBi hetero‐clusters were constructed on hierarchical porous carbon nanofiber scaffold, which integrate significant interatomic charge transfer and accelerated water dissociation kinetics, enabling highly enhanced electrocatalytic alkaline hydrogen evolution while maintaining stable, long‐term operation in practical anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzers.








ABSTRACT
Controlling the size and interfacial structure of bimetallic hetero‐clusters below two nanometers represents a key challenge in catalyst design due to their thermodynamic tendency to undergo sintering and phase segregation. This work presents a dual spatial confinement strategy to synthesize uniformly dispersed, sub‐nanometer RuBi bimetallic hetero‐clusters embedded within porous carbon nanofibers (RuBi HCs/PCNFs). The synthetic approach utilizes the internal pores of metal‐organic frameworks as primary nano‐reactors, coupled with an electrospun polymer matrix as a secondary physical barrier, preventing metal migration and coalescence during high‐temperature pyrolysis. We employ the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) as a probe to evaluate the efficacy of this structural design. Characterizations and theoretical analysis show that the atomic proximity and electronic interactions between Ru and Bi optimize intermediate adsorption and accelerate the rate‐determining water dissociation step. Benefiting from these structural and electronic advantages, the RuBi HCs/PCNFs catalyst delivers enhanced electrocatalytic HER activity and robust operational durability. When evaluated in an anion exchange membrane (AEM) water electrolyzer, the catalyst demonstrates stable, long‐term operation, showcasing the practical utility of the hetero‐cluster configuration. This study demonstrates the feasibility of utilizing dual spatial confinement to construct stable, sub‐nanometer bimetallic platforms for electrocatalytic applications.

title: W–H Bond‐Mediated “Anti‐Overoxidation Valve”: 100% Formaldehyde Selectivity Among Detected Products in Photocatalytic Methane‐to‐Formaldehyde Conversion
content:
To suppress overoxidation in photocatalytic CH4‐to‐HCHO conversion, we engineer W‐H bonds on H/WO2.72 (hydrogenated). These bonds are a kinetic valve, preferentially cleaved with ·OOH over C‐H bonds of HCOOH, the resulting H* reduces *HCOOH to *HCHO, blocking CO2. Hydrogenation narrows the band gap and weakens HCHO adsorption. The H/WO2.72 catalyst achieves 100% selectivity toward formaldehyde among all detected carbon‐containing products, with a production rate of 30.94 µmol·h−1 and excellent operational stability. This M‐H bond strategy is universal (TiO2, ZnO).








ABSTRACT
Direct photocatalytic conversion of methane to formaldehyde is highly efficient, avoiding energy‐intensive methanol oxidation. However, its selectivity and activity are severely limited by uncontrollable over‐oxidation: Formaldehyde has lower C‐H dissociation energy than methane, prone to deep overoxidation to CO2. Herein, we report H/WO2.72 hydrogenated nonstoichiometric tungsten oxide photocatalyst. At ambient temperature, it attains 100% HCHO selectivity over all detectable carbonaceous products at 30.94 µmol·h−1, with 11‐fold higher activity than commercial WO3 and outperforming most conventional photocatalysts. Operando spectroscopic studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that surface W‐H bonds act as a kinetically gated “Anti‐Overoxidation valve,” W–H bonds are preferentially cleaved by reactive oxygen species (·OOH), as they are thermodynamically weaker than the C–H bonds in HCHO and its over‐oxidation intermediate (*HCOOH). Then the generated hydrogen radicals (H*) drive a reverse reduction pathway to convert the *HCOOH back to *HCHO, interrupting deep oxidation. Concurrently, hydrogenation optimizes the electronic structure of WO2.72, lowering the HCHO desorption barrier to facilitate timely product release. This work provides a dynamic strategy for complete selectivity in catalytic CH4 conversion, emphasizing the value of precise kinetic pathway modulation for methane valorization.

title: Enhanced Electrochemical C–N Coupling for Glycine Synthesis via an Active Hydrogen Pump
content:
An In–Bi catalyst is developed for efficient electrochemical synthesis of glycine via C–N coupling of oxalic acid and nitrate. Oxophilic In sites act as an “active hydrogen pump” to accelerate H2O dissociation and supply *H, while the Bi matrix promotes glyoxylic acid oxime (GAO) adsorption. The synergistic effect enables a glycine Faradaic efficiency of 83.3% and an industrial‐level current density of 361.3 mA cm−2.








ABSTRACT
Direct electrochemical C–N coupling of abundant carbon and nitrogen feedstocks offers a sustainable route to glycine synthesis, yet achieving high efficiency remains challenging. Here, we develop an In–Bi catalyst by incorporating oxophilic indium (In) into a bismuth (Bi) matrix. During the co‐reduction of oxalic acid and NO3−, the In–Bi catalyst delivers an exceptional Faradaic efficiency toward glycine (FEGlycine) of 83.3% with an industrial‐level current density of 361.3 mA cm−2, together with a glycine production rate of 4.3 mol h−1 gcat.−1. It outperforms pristine Bi and previously reported state‐of‐the‐art catalysts. Large‐scale glycine electrosynthesis is further demonstrated over a 10 cm2 In–Bi electrode, achieving a total current of 1.5 A with FEGlycine of 68.5% and yielding 1.4 g of glycine in 6 h. Mechanistically, oxalic acid and NO3− first form glyoxylic acid oxime (GAO). Subsequently, In sites act as an “active hydrogen pump” to accelerate H2O dissociation, providing abundant surface‐active hydrogen (*H) for efficient GAO hydrogenation to glycine. Meanwhile, the incorporation of In modulates the electronic structure of the Bi matrix, enhancing GAO adsorption and electron transfer. The synergistic regulation of *H supply and electronic structure accelerates the conversion of GAO to glycine, resulting in superior performance of In–Bi.
