title: Cofactor‐Inspired Second‐Sphere Engineering of Artificial Metalloenzymes for Neutral Ammonia Synthesis
content:
A cofactor‐inspired nanozyme featuring spatially coupled yet functionally differentiated catalytic sites within individual Cu clusters was developed for efficient neutral NO3RR and Zn−NO3− battery. Exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase to promote nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu‐1S] motifs orchestrate the second‐sphere hydration microenvironment, facilitating PCET and active hydrogen relay during downstream nitrite hydrogenation. 








ABSTRACT
Constructing artificial metalloenzymes with precisely positioned metal centers and tailored second‐sphere microenvironments remains challenging in replicating the hierarchical catalytic functions of natural enzymes. Here, we report a cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering strategy to construct an artificial nanozyme, CuS1/CN, featuring atomically defined [3Cu−1S] motifs selectively anchored to ultrasmall Cu clusters (∼0.73 nm) within a mesoporous nitrogen‐doped carbon framework. This architecture establishes enzyme‐like catalytic compartmentalization without compromising active‐site accessibility: exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase for nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu−1S] motifs function as cofactor‐like centers that orchestrate interfacial hydration, facilitating proton‐coupled electron transfer and hydrogen relay during downstream hydrogenation. The engineered second‐sphere microenvironment overcomes the intrinsic *NO2‐to‐*NO2H bottleneck and shifts the rate‐determining step to *NH2O‐to‐*NH2OH conversion with a substantially reduced energy barrier. Consequently, CuS1/CN enables highly efficient and selective ammonia electrosynthesis under neutral conditions at industrially relevant current densities with long‐term stability. Its integration into a Zn−NO3− battery further enables simultaneous nitrate conversion and electricity generation. This work establishes cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering as a general strategy for designing artificial enzymes with programmable catalytic microenvironments beyond conventional active‐site engineering.

title: In Situ Product Separation Suppresses Self‐Poisoning in 2‐Butanol Electrooxidation
content:
Alloy‐catalyst engineering and reaction–rectification enable selective 2‐butanol electrooxidation to methyl ethyl ketone (MEK) while mitigating product‐induced inhibition. The integrated system continuously operates at 14 A and approximately 1.3 V, delivering MEK at 99% purity alongside hydrogen and demonstrating a promising strategy for coupled electrocatalysis and product separation.








ABSTRACT
Replacing the oxygen evolution reaction with the electrooxidation of 2‐butanol (SBA) offers an energy‐efficient route to co‐production of hydrogen and methyl ethyl ketone (MEK), yet achieving selective MEK formation while maintaining sustained operation remains challenging because of sluggish anodic kinetics and product accumulation. Here, we integrate alloy‐catalyst engineering with reaction–rectification to address these coupled catalytic and process‐level limitations. A self‐supported PdAu/NF anode exploits Pd–Au ligand interactions to regulate the adsorption of SBA, surface hydroxyl species and MEK, thereby suppressing C─C bond cleavage and facilitating product desorption. The optimized PdAu/NF catalyst delivers 300 mA cm−2 at 0.74 V versus RHE. Despite weakened MEK adsorption, accumulated MEK and MEK‐derived intermediates inhibit SBA oxidation on PdAu and hydrogen evolution on Pt. At the process level, membrane‐free PdAu/NF||Pt/NF electrode arrays are integrated with reaction–rectification, enabling continuous MEK removal, recovery and SBA recycling. This in situ product separation mitigates product accumulation and its inhibitory effects, enabling continuous electrolysis at 14 A with a cell voltage of approximately 1.3 V over 10 h. The integrated system produces MEK with 99% purity while simultaneously generating hydrogen, highlighting the potential of coupling molecular‐level catalyst regulation with process‐level product management for MEK and hydrogen co‐production.

title: Mechanocatalytic Upcycling of Diverse Plastic Wastes via an Fe/SiO2 Catalyst
content:
We report the mechanocatalytic conversion of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and their mixtures into valuable hydrogen and methane gases on an iron species‐dispersed silica catalyst, achieving almost 100% conversion under mild conditions. No expensive components, toxic chemicals, or energy‐intensive thermal conditions are needed.








ABSTRACT
Upcycling plastic waste into high‐value chemicals is an attractive pathway for the sustainable development of human society. Here, we demonstrate the mechanocatalytic conversion of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and their mixtures into valuable hydrogen (H2) and methane (CH4) gases on an iron (Fe) species‐dispersed silica (SiO2) catalyst, achieving almost 100% conversion under mild conditions. During the mechanocatalytic process, Fe species from the milling balls were anchored to the surface of pristine SiO2 nanoparticles, forming the Fe/SiO2 catalyst. Simultaneously, the Fe and Si sites in the Fe/SiO2 catalyst synergistically facilitate the C─H bond activation and C─C bond cleavage pathways, enabling a favorable dehydrogenation‒cracking‒hydrogenation process to produce commercially valuable H2 and CH4. Notably, this catalytic system also exhibits exceptional versatility in processing mixed plastic wastes without requiring prior sorting, while maintaining robust cycling stability. No expensive components, toxic chemicals, or energy‐intensive thermal conditions are needed.

title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
content:
A bifunctional metal–organic framework, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers and viologen electron mediators to couple energy transfer (EnT) and electron transfer (ET) processes within a single framework. This dual‐channel O2 activation strategy generates both type I and type II reactive oxygen species without requiring redox‐active metal centers, leading to potent photodynamic antitumor efficacy with no obvious systemic toxicity.








ABSTRACT
Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O2‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO2+) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

title: Unraveling the Crystallization Kinetics of High‐Quality Perovskite Quantum Dots via Microfluidic Synthesis System
content:
A glass‐chip microfluidic platform probes crystallization kinetics of pure‐red CsPb(Br/I)3 perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) at 0.1 s resolution, yielding high‐performance PQDs (λ = 623 nm, PLQY = 91.8%, FWHM = 29.6 nm). Time‐resolved TEM reveals ligand‐governed 1D, 2D and 3D evolution within 10 s. These PQDs excel in display backlights and flexible films, enabling controllable synthesis of high‐quality perovskite optoelectronic materials.








ABSTRACT
Precisely controlling the crystallization kinetics of perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) during synthesis is essential for achieving high optoelectronic performance and for investigating their intrinsic nucleation and growth mechanisms. However, PQDs synthesis typically proceeds via a hot‐injection batch approach within few seconds, making it highly challenging to control and gain fundamental insight into their crystallization kinetics. Here, we present the microfluidic synthesis of PQDs with precise control of reaction condition within 10 s using a microfluidic chip featured excellent temporal resolution and high‐throughput, thereby allowing direct investigation and elucidation of the fast crystallization kinetics. The rapid and precise control of reaction conditions enabled the microfluidic synthesis of pure‐red PQDs with record performance (623 nm, PLQY of 91.8%), using only oleic acid and oleylamine as surface ligands. The reaction and crystallization kinetics was monitored with 0.1 second temporal resolution, which infers a plausible sequential growth scenario for high‐quality nanocrystal: initially rapid nanowires formation, followed by partial dissolution‐reorganization into nanosheets, and ultimately evolving into a cubic‐shaped nanocrystals. The high‐quality PQDs was further integrated as a color‐conversion layer of display backlight, demonstrating outstanding red‐color purity and potential for flexible display.
